overall_reason: The traction chart's bar heights do not match its own labels ($8k is drawn at 4.75px per $1k, $81k at 2.96px), and its title says 34% month on month while the labelled values grow 47% to 88% a month, under the deck's blue-to-magenta gradient.

score.reason: T-CHART-TEXT-MATCH and T-HONEST-SCALE fail on the traction bars (DVZ-005, DVZ-004), T-DATA-INK on gradient bars (DVZ-006), and T-STAT-TILE on the market tiles (DVZ-013).

findings.where: section.slide:nth-of-type(7) > div.traction-bar, 1920 (contact sheet #1, 1696 by 241px at y7036; tiles/1920-06.png)
findings.evidence: The bars are labelled $8k, $15k, $23k, $36k, $55k and $81k. On the tile they measure 38, 67, 100, 144, 192 and 240px tall from a shared baseline. That is 4.75px per $1k for October and 2.96px per $1k for March. If drawn to scale from March, the October bar would be 24px. If drawn to scale from October, March would be 385px.
findings.before: Box-drawn bars whose heights are compressed toward the top, so the later months look smaller than their labels.
findings.after: Draw each bar's height in proportion to its value from $0, so March is about 10 times October, and keep the value labels on top.
findings.why: On an investor deck the bars are the traction claim. Heights that do not follow the labels make the curve look steadier than the figures say.

findings.where: slide 7 title 'Traction · 6 months, growing 34% MoM.' over the same bars, 1920 (tiles/1920-06.png)
findings.evidence: From the bar labels, month-on-month growth is 88% (8 to 15), 53%, 57%, 53% and 47% (55 to 81). The compound rate from $8k to $81k over five months is about 59% a month. None of these is 34%. The chart also never names its measure. Only the ask slide says '$81K to $500K MRR'.
findings.before: A headline growth rate that the chart under it does not show, over bars with no metric name.
findings.after: Make the title match the figures, for example 'MRR up from $8k to $81k in six months, about 59% a month', and add 'MRR, $k' as the chart's unit line.
findings.why: An investor who checks the arithmetic finds the headline and the bars disagree, and then distrusts both. Lens-integrity owns whether the figures are real.

findings.where: the traction bars and the stat figures on slides 4, 5 and 9, 1920 (contact sheet #1 to #9)
findings.evidence: Every bar is filled with the deck's diagonal gradient from blue to magenta. The sweep's gradient hit (SLP-007) reports a hue span of 50 degrees (#3b5bff, #7a46ff, #d94cff), and it covers the stat figures as well.
findings.before: Gradient-filled data bars, so each bar changes colour from its bottom-left to its top-right.
findings.after: Fill the bars in one flat brand blue, with March in the accent if it is the focal month.
findings.why: A colour change inside a bar suggests a second variable that does not exist, and it adds ink to every mark.
findings.root: the deck's .gradient fill token used on text, figures and chart marks

findings.where: section.slide:nth-of-type(5) > div.grid.g3 > div.metric, 1920 (contact sheet #2 to #4, y4932; tiles/1920-04.png)
findings.evidence: The market slide shows '41M developers worldwide who use an AI coding agent daily', '$92B TAM · design + prototyping software spend' and '38% YoY growth in AI-assisted software teams'. The tiles give no year for any figure, and 38% does not say what grew (team count, or spend). The sweep's stat_band hit (INT-007) covers the missing sources.
findings.before: Three figures of three kinds (a count of people, a market size and a growth rate) with no period.
findings.after: Give each tile its year and measure ('$92B, 2026 global spend on design and prototyping software'), and add a source line under the row.
findings.why: A market slide is read for scale and date. Without a year, the figures cannot be compared or checked.

findings.evidence: The ask slide says '$2.5M' in the headline ('Raising $2.5M seed.') and again as the first tile, and says '$500K MRR' in the body and again in the third tile.
findings.before: Two of the three tiles repeat figures already set in larger type on the same slide.
findings.after: Keep the headline and body, and turn the tile row into the terms only: 'SAFE, post-money cap $18M' and '18 months of runway'.
findings.why: Repeated figures make the slide look full without telling the investor anything new.
